title: Library code awaits with ConfigureAwait(false)
statement: Async methods in `AgentOrchestrator.CodeQuality` (the reusable core library, as opposed to ASP.NET Core request-handling code in `QualityStudio.Api`) call `.ConfigureAwait(false)` on every `await` of a library-internal or BCL task.
rationale: The core package is documented as usable standalone ('the package stays usable standalone... write meta JSONs, drive the CLI runner'), which means its async methods can run under a host with a capturing `SynchronizationContext`. `ConfigureAwait(false)` keeps the continuation off that context, avoiding needless context-switch overhead and a class of deadlocks in synchronous-over-asynchronous callers outside this repo's own ASP.NET Core host, where it is unnecessary but harmless.

good.caption: Every await in the review pipeline uses ConfigureAwait(false).

bad.code:
var fileContent = await BuildSubjectContentAsync(subjectPaths, files, request.Level, cancellationToken);
var sensorEvidence = await CollectSensorEvidenceAsync(request, root, subjectPaths, cancellationToken);
bad.caption: Same awaits without ConfigureAwait(false) in library code.

changelog.summary: Initial rule, grounded in ReviewRunner.cs's consistent ConfigureAwait(false) usage. autofixable: true (a Roslyn analyzer/codefix such as CA2007 can insert it mechanically).
